title: Chapter 8: Generics and Type-Safe Reuse
description: Preserve useful type relationships in reusable APIs without raw types or broad casts. Learners implement generic classes and methods, reason from allowed operations to bounds, apply PECS at producer and consumer boundaries, explain wildcard capture and erasure, and isolate unavoidable unchecked interoperability behind tested adapters.

lessons.title: Generic classes, interfaces, methods, and raw types

exercises.title: Generic classes, interfaces, methods, and raw types: concept check
choices: The stored and returned value type
hints: Recall that the type parameter T ties the constructor argument to what get() returns, so the compiler enforces that relationship instead of forcing a cast at retrieval.

exercises.title: Invariance, wildcard capture, and PECS: concept check
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Why can't List<Integer> be assigned to List<Number>?
choices: It would permit inserting incompatible Number values
hints: Recall invariance: if List<Integer> could be used as List<Number>, code holding that List<Number> reference could insert a Double, silently corrupting the underlying Integer list.

lessons.title: Upper, lower, multiple, and recursive bounds

exercises.title: Upper, lower, multiple, and recursive bounds: concept check
exercises.instructionMarkdown: What does a Comparable bound enable inside a generic method?
hints: Recall that `T extends Comparable<? super T>` is what gives the method body a checked compareTo call to invoke; without it, `a.compareTo(b)` would not compile.

lessons.title: Type erasure, bridge methods, and heap pollution

exercises.title: Type erasure, bridge methods, and heap pollution: concept check
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Can instanceof List<String> prove element types at runtime?
choices: Yes; every element is checked automatically
No; that parameterized runtime test is unavailable
hints: Recall that erasure removes type-argument information at runtime, so only the raw `instanceof List<?>` test is available; a parameterized instanceof check cannot be compiled.

lessons.title: Designing readable and usable generic APIs

exercises.title: Designing readable and usable generic APIs: concept check
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Why avoid wildcard return types when a precise return type is truthful?
choices: They make callers manage unnecessary unknown types
hints: Recall that a wildcard return type forces every caller to work with an unknown type parameter, even when the implementation actually knows and could promise a precise type.

exercises.title: Generics and Type-Safe Reuse: professional judgment
exercises.instructionMarkdown: A generic API needs only to read values. What should guide its parameter bound?
choices: The producer operations the algorithm needs
Adding every available interface as a bound

exercises.title: Chapter 8 implementation lab: copyRange
exercises.instructionMarkdown:
Implement `copyRange`. Return values from start inclusive to end exclusive; clamp both bounds into the array. Write the precondition and boundary table first, keep the method deterministic, and do not print.

Input is non-null. Clamp each bound to 0..length; return an empty new array when the clamped end is not greater than start.
hints: Clamp both start and end into the valid 0..length range before computing the slice, not after indexing with the raw values.
Trace the public example plus a boundary where the clamped range collapses to empty, such as a negative start or an end at or before the clamped start.

exercises.title: Producer and consumer bounds
exercises.instructionMarkdown: `copy` declares a single invariant type parameter `T` for both the source and destination lists, but the call site passes a `List<Integer>` source and a `List<Number>` destination, which cannot both satisfy one `T` — so the program does not compile and never writes `[1, 2]`. Repair the method's bounds using PECS (producer extends, consumer super) so it accepts this call while keeping the demonstrated types, and explain why the wildcard bounds fix the mismatch; do not replace it with a hard-coded print. Output tests verify the result; preserving the intended operation requires source review.
hints: Use source producer and destination consumer bounds while retaining generic type safety.
